response.sql: WITH hands AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), '') AS bats, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS player_count FROM player_award pa JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pa.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), '')), shares AS (SELECT bats, player_count, player_count * 1.0 / SUM(player_count) OVER () AS share FROM hands), avg_share AS (SELECT bats, player_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT bats, player_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM avg_share WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC

assumptions.assumption: Blank, whitespace-only, and NULL bats values are all merged into a single group labeled with an empty string.

The total award-winning players across all hands is the sum of per-hand distinct counts. This equals the overall distinct count because each player has exactly one bats value (player_id is assumed unique in player).
The share is a fraction between 0 and 1, not a percentage. The average is taken across the hand groups present, with no rounding.
